bug_semantics: Unauthenticated time-based blind SQL injection in Tainacan's geocoordinate WP_Query filter. REST GET handlers copy request['geoquery'] into WP_Query args; GeoCoordinate_Helper::posts_where then interpolates attacker-controlled point, distance, key, and polygon values into ST_Distance_Sphere / ST_GEOMFROMTEXT fragments with no escaping or $wpdb->prepare. A public collection items request can therefore append SQL and extract database contents. CVE-2026-6230 / Wordfence: all versions <= 1.0.3; the sink first shipped in 0.20.0.
flaw_origin: 2dc5cf5c6f6eef3e24fcc07853d5e092766b6823 (2022-12-23, feat: add geoCoordinateHelper to processed geoquery #692) created class-tainacan-geocoordinate-helper.php and wired geoquery through REST_Items_Controller. posts_where DISTANCE/CONTAINS cases concatenated $params['point'], $params['distance'], $params['key'], and $params['polygon'] directly into SQL. Those concatenations are absent from parent 1ab2f8972aa2b002dc97fcee25c0551065cf2069 and were unchanged until the 2026 patch.

Single-parent non-merge feature commit; no reconstructable public members.

Attack path still live at tag 1.0.3: helper posts_where still concatenates unsanitized geoquery fields (no $wpdb->prepare); REST_Items_Controller copies request geoquery at the 1.0.3 file's lines 699-701. get_items_permissions_check returns true for readable collections, so the GET collection items route is unauthenticated for public collections.

reasoning: CVE-2026-6230 is a published Wordfence CWE-89 record, not withdrawn or rejected. The sink is GeoCoordinate_Helper::posts_where concatenating REST-supplied geoquery fields into MySQL spatial predicates. That function and the REST geoquery pass-through were first written in 2dc5cf5c6f6eef3e24fcc07853d5e092766b6823; the parent tree lacks the helper file and any ST_Distance_Sphere/geoquery SQL, and no later commit rewrote the concatenation before 579d28d7752b27ed3407f5197abb6349b3efc3c9. The BIC is therefore the smallest public first-write, not a move, refactor, revert, or squash aggregate. It precedes affected tag 1.0.3 (from first release 0.20.0); the direct fix lands in 1.1.0, matching WPScan's patched boundary even though Wordfence's upper bound is the last vulnerable release 1.0.3. The BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI trailers, so authorship is NOT_AI.
